motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default for state changes, FLIP re-rank, hero rise, press and thread draw-in.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Declared on :root but unused in CSS; the cloth reweave uses its own cubic in-out in JS.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active state on buttons, the switch and Copy; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Color and background transitions on links, buttons and steps.

motion.name: thread-draw
motion.value: scaleX 0 to 1 from the left, 220-240ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Ledger hover thread and stepper progress threads.

motion.name: flip-rerank
motion.purpose: Insight board rows when weights change; skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.value: opacity 0 and translateY(10px) to rest, 700ms ease-out; delays 0/60/140/220/280/340/400ms
motion.purpose: Hero claim lines, sub and ledger entries. Reduced motion: 400ms fade.

motion.name: field-light
motion.purpose: Lens ticket fields as the stepper reaches them.

motion.name: cloth-reweave
motion.value: 1.1s cubic in-out sweep rising up the screen with a ragged 3-thread edge; 140ms hover-out delay
motion.purpose: Motif change on section change or ledger/door hover. Reduced motion: instant swap, one frame.

motion.name: cloth-pose
motion.purpose: Per-section tilt, offset, billow and side shade.

motion.name: cloth-lift
motion.value: 16-point pointer trail, gaussian lift amplitude 0.55, decay exp(-1.5 dt), lit-gold glow
motion.purpose: Threads lift and glow under the pointer, then settle. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: cloth-weave-scroll
motion.purpose: The cloth advances with scroll. Off under reduced motion.

cloth.renderer: Three.js ShaderMaterial on an 18x12 plane, 20 threads per unit; DPR capped at 1.5, steps down to 0.75 after 45 slow frames

narrative.overview:
The page is one length of Malay songket cloth rendered in WebGL behind every section: an oxblood silk ground, warp and weft threads you can see at full size, and a gold supplementary weft that weaves a different motif for each tool. Everything in the DOM reads as something laid on that cloth: woven labels with a gold selvedge along their top edge, single gold threads as rules, and figures set in tabular numerals with their source file printed directly beneath. The cloth sets the scene. The numbers are the content, and no part of the weave is ever drawn over a figure.

Density is editorial and unhurried. The column runs about 760px, sections are separated by up to 180px of open cloth, and every panel has one job. Gold carries names, actions and results. Silver carries misses, disputes, withdrawals and declines, set in the same type size and weight as the gold beside it. The system is flat, rectangular and threadlike. Glass, gradients on surfaces and rounded cards play no part in it.

Motion follows the loom. The cloth billows slowly, reweaves its motif in a ragged sweep when the visitor changes tool, lifts and lights threads under the pointer, and changes pose as each section scrolls into view. Under reduced motion the whole scene renders as a single still frame.
keyCharacteristics: One oxblood ground for the whole page (#2a0910), with darker woven panels laid on it
Gold weft for names, actions and results, silver for misses at equal size
Reem Kufi display on a woven, geometric grid. Hanken Grotesk for reading, JetBrains Mono only for code, paths, formulas and tool names
Every figure is real text in tabular numerals, with its source line directly under it
1px gold threads for rules, a 7px pucuk rebung selvedge on panels, 2px corners at most
A WebGL songket behind everything that weaves one motif per product

rules.name: The Equal Thread Rule
rules.body: A miss is set in silver at the same size, weight and position as the gold win beside it. Silver is never smaller, lighter or pushed into a footnote.

rules.name: The Two Metals Rule
rules.body: Gold and silver are the only accent colors. A new state is expressed as gold (passed, computed, won) or silver (missed, disputed, declined). Never add a third hue.

rules.name: The One Cloth Rule
rules.body: Every surface is a shade of the same oxblood. Panels get darker than the ground and are never lighter, tinted or translucent.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for strings a machine reads: code, file paths, formulas, tool names, raw passages. Prose, labels and figures never use it.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Any element holding a number uses tabular numerals, so figures align in tables and stay put when a re-rank or stepper changes them.

rules.name: The Cloth Carries Depth Rule
rules.body: The 3D is the WebGL cloth. DOM surfaces get at most the label drop and never use glass, blur or glow.

dos: Do put the source file or report name directly under every figure, in dusk at 0.72rem to 0.8rem, mono when it is a bare path.
Do set a miss in silver at the same size and weight as the win next to it (The Equal Thread Rule).
Do lay new evidence inside a woven label panel with the pucuk rebung selvedge, on label fill, with a 1px faint gold border.
Do use 1px gold threads for every rule and 2px gold threads, drawn in from the left, for active or hover marks.
Do give a new product its own songket motif in the cloth shader and map its section and ledger entry to it.
Do keep press feedback at `scale(0.97)` and state transitions at 160ms to 240ms on cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), and drop both under reduced motion.
Do keep buttons, switches, steps, ledger and nav links at 44px tall or more (36px for the in-header Copy button).
donts: Don't use glass, backdrop blur, glow or translucent panels. Panels are opaque woven labels.
Don't add a third accent hue. A state is gold or silver.
Don't set prose, labels or figures in JetBrains Mono.
Don't round corners past 2px, except the range thumb.
Don't place the cloth's gold motif behind a figure without a scrim or shade. The hero scrim and the per-section side shade exist so text never sits on bright weft.
Don't let a three-letter tool code stand alone above a heading. It always sits beside its tool name.
